ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure shows the complete Nyquist curve in the G(s)H(s)-plane, the horizontal axis is labeled Re GH, and the vertical axis is labeled j Im GH; the origin 0 is marked near the intersection of the two axes, and the critical point (-1,j0) is also on the real axis, located to the left of the origin and marked by an arrow. The curve contains a relatively large outer closed loop and an inner small loop near the real axis. From the graph it can be counted that: the net winding number of the curve around the origin is 0; the net winding number of the curve around the critical point (-1,j0) is two clockwise encirclements. Reasoning: According to the specified method, first use the origin winding number relation W_0 = Z_{GH} - P_{GH}. It is known that G(s)H(s) has one zero in the right half-plane, so Z_{GH}=1; in the figure, the net winding number around the origin W_0=0, therefore 0 = 1 - P_{GH}, obtaining P_{GH}=1. Then use the Nyquist relation W_{-1}=Z_{CL}-P_{GH} for the critical point (-1,j0). In the figure there are two clockwise windings around (-1,j0), that is W_{-1}=2, so Z_{CL}=W_{-1}+P_{GH}=2+1=3. Therefore the number of poles of the closed-loop system in the right half s-plane is 3.
